newsitem.title: UK: POLL-UK rates expected to stick at 6.75 pct-4CAST.
newsitem.headline: POLL-UK rates expected to stick at 6.75 pct-4CAST.

text.p: Britain is likely to keep interest rates on hold when the Bank of England's monetary policy committee (MPC) meets next week, a survey showed on Friday.
Financial analysts 4CAST canvassed 71 dealing rooms across Europe and found that 44 respondents, or 62 percent, expected the MPC to leave rates unchanged at 6.75 percent.
The 4CAST results conflict with those of a Reuters poll of 23 London-based economists published on Thursday, which favoured a 25 basis point increase to 7.0 percent.
But the findings of both surveys pointed to further rises before the end of the year, with 48 percent of 4CAST respondents expecting rates to peak at 7.0 percent in 1997.
Sterling's recent wobble failed to dampen expectations that it was set to climb higher.
4CAST asked 70 dealers to predict the 1997 peak for sterling against the mark and found that 47 saw another rally, with the predictions ranging from the 3.0880 peak reached on July 23 to 3.30 marks.
The median expectation for the 1997 high was 3.10 marks, with the mean slightly higher at 3.1150 marks.

More than half the 70 respondents predicted a further 25 basis point rise in the U.S. Fed Funds rate to 5.75 percent. Dollar-mark predictions from 71 contributors for the 1997 peak ranged from 1.8490 already seen on July 28 and 2.05. The median was 1.90 marks.
